Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-210 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText:
Pro:  Good value; Cooks well; color selections (red!)
Con: Purchase of additional bulk LP flow adapter kit

I purchased this grill on-line last month.  It was packaged extremely well and easy enough to assemble (2-3 hours at a very leisurely pace).  Because we have a large LP tank in ground at our new house and had the builder run a line to our deck I was anxious to hook up my grill to the line and finally avoid the need to purchase 20lb propane tanks (you need an extra one because the propane always runs out while you are in the middle of grilling) and drive 60 minutes round trip to town for refills. 

What could be easier?  Perhaps inclusion of the bulk LP flow adapter kit?  Apparently, if you buy the natural gas version of the Spirit II E-210, the hose is included (because you cannot buy small tanks of natural gas, and Weber assumes you have a natural gas line nearby to connect) but if you buy the LP version Weber assumes you will use 20 lb propane tanks.  The conversion kit is a separate purchase.  To my knowledge the kit can be bought only from Weber, and they will sell you one only after you register your grill (probably to safeguard you from buying the wrong item) which means you cannot receive your grill, assemble it and cook the same day.

So after registering my grill online (very easy process) and shelling out an addition $60 for the conversion kit and waiting a week for it to arrive, I eagerly open the package and instructions and see....PROFESSIONAL INSTALLER INSTRUCTIONS (THIS INSTALLATION SHOULD BE DONE ONLY BY A LICENSED PROFESSIONAL...).  Now, this has me thinking, best case I pay for an install ($85.31 plus tax from my local propane dealer) or worst case, I try it myself and blow up the house, injure myself, or maybe ruin my new grill.  After talking the situation over with several more knowledgeable folks I come to the conclusion this is language that Weber legal beagles insist be included to cover their butts and, if I use common sense, I can do the install myself despite my plumbing inexperience.

OK, ready to go.  I refer to the instructions and notice there are three different conversion kits depending on which model grill you buy.  All three kits, however, show the same five components: 1) quick-disconnect--this is at one end of the hose included in my kit; 2) a 3/8" threaded pipe nipple; 3) a reducing coupling, 3/8" - 1/2"; 4) a 1/2" threaded pipe nipple; and 5) a locking shutoff--this I see is at the end of the gas line the builder installed.

Being the logical guy I am, I presume the kit contains the threaded pipe nipples and reducing coupling. Nope, nowhere to be found.  Is this an oversight, or am I supposed to purchase these?  Well, all three kits show the need for these so they must be included.  Check again,. Nope, not in the box.  I call up Weber Customer Service, explain what is missing and am told, "I'm so sorry.  We can take care of that."  The person tells me they will send another kit, and not to bother returning what I just opened since it is not economic to do so. Cool, but I do have to wait another week to grill.

Another week goes by and my package comes.....with the hose only!  Now it is evident to me the kit does NOT INCLUDE the two threaded pipe nipples nor the reducing coupling and the Customer Service people have systems that do not inform them of the kit contents since neither person I spoke with (one for the original order, another for the replacement) mentioned this additional purchase to me.  In fairness, the Customer Service folks were very pleasant and professional, so I believe this is a Weber training failure.

Since we do not live real close to a home improvement store I waited until our weekly trip to town to purchase $20 of pipe nipple and reducing coupling hardware and pipe thread compound to make sure my connections were secure.  Got out a couple of wrenches, watched a You Tube video how to disconnect the LP hose and regulator that I had assembled originally, (honestly, this was the most difficult step--once it was off, there was only one way to make everything fit together) I hand-tightened everything as a dry run, then took it all apart and reassembled with the pipe thread compound and cranked it down with my wrenches, making sure not to over tighten.

Waited 24 hours just to be sure the pipe compound had dried and formed a good seal, sprayed soapy water over all the connections and...opened...the...shutoff valve to the LP gas line.  NO BUBBLES!!!!

Now for the moment of truth.  Reviewed the ignition instructions. Turned the dial, pressed the ignition button...and...and...3-4 seconds later..a soft whoosh.  Turned the other burner dial and another soft whoosh.  Held my hand over the grill and...heat.  It worked!!!

First cooking experience was salmon. Fired up the left burner only and after 7-8 minutes the thermometer was "only" 300 degrees.  Was only intending to use one side of the grill so I was a bit disappointed that I would have to use the other burner to get to 400-450, but 3 minutes later I was at 500 degrees so this baby heats well!!!  Turned down both dials to halfway and the temp quickly dropped to 450.  Put on the salmon and came back in 7 minutes to see the temp was back at 500.  Hmm...very efficient....guess I didn't need both burners after all and the grill temp is much hotter than the temp near the lid where the thermometer is.  Anyhow, the salmon came out perfectly done. It was all in foil so I did not have a chance to evaluate the grease drip system or other features. Steak tonight!  That will be a bit more messy. 

So, all in all, I'm happy with the grill, but I did have to spend $80 more than I thought would be necessary.  On the other hand, I saved myself $90 of install costs and probably $80 on propane tanks that I no longer need.

Results.ReviewText:
Bought the grill 2 months ago. The positives are it's easy to put together, easy to lite, easy to move, and nice small size. The negatives- you can tell where they cut corners to save cost (in the lid and the frame shelf), and the lowest temperature it can hold with one burner on is 275 dents. I was hoping I'd be able to use the grill as a pseudo smoker but it can't get that low.

There's one other thing, I don't know if it's an issue or not, or just how it operates, but there a whistling sounds that flickers when the burgers are turned between the lowest and quarter power. It almost sounds like the gas is about to go out (although it's a new tank).

I've glossed over the good parts of the grill as many others have mentioned them, but this is a good grill and have enjoyed cooking on it multiple times from fish to burgers to pizza, it's done everything well.

We are a family of 4 and have had the big 4 burner grills in the past and realized how much of a waste it is to just have a huge cooking area when not needing it for just cooking a dinner... And the off chance of hosting a party, so we got smaller to accommodate 95% of our grilling needs.

Results.ReviewText: I bought this a few months ago and absolutely love it!  Looked at other BBQ’s but kept coming back to this one because of its quality. Results.Title: Love it!

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-210 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText: I've always had cheaper grills in the past. They worked without fail. I decided to upgrade and see what something that cost most would do. My new Weber grill works so well I can't take any credit on how the food turns out. It's design is amazing. The food never burns even when I start to panic because I forgot about it. I can't ask for anything more when it comes to performance. It cost more, worth every penny.
Results.Title: Best Grill Ever

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-210 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText: Bought this grill to down-size from a four burner grill.  Great heat production and even distribution.  Had a 3-burner Weber in past and remembered its flawless functioning.  Excellent little grill.
Results.Title: Spirit II E-210 Gas Grill

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-210 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText: This grill is extremely sturdy yet light and easy to assemble. Heats up fast and maintains temperature well. The grates are well made, solid and easy to clean. It is nice that there are two burners but three flavorizer bars to make the grill even regardless of food placement. I have only cooked burgers on it so far but it is already far superior to other grills I have had. Simple but solid and works great every time. Perfect. Definitely a Weber customer for the foreseeable future. Would definitely recommend this grill
Results.Title: Great Grill at a Great Price Point

44010001.Name: Spirit II E-210 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
44010001.Description:
Open the door to the world of grilling with crazy good food and friends coming together. Equipped with the powerful GS4 grilling system, this two burner gas grill is your entry to the Weber family and to everyday grilling. The compact open-cart design and the practical folding side table makes it fit even on small spaces, and you have all the basics you need to get familiar with gas grilling. So whether it’s a busy Monday or a relaxed Sunday – invite a couple of friends over, push the ignition and enjoy the special atmosphere that surrounds the grill.


 This product requires assembly.

44020001.Name: Spirit II E-210 Gas Grill
44020001.Description: Open your door to the world of grilling with the sleek Spirit II E-210 gas grill. This two burner grill is built to fit small spaces, and packed with features such as the powerful GS4 grilling system, iGrill capability, and convenient side tables for placing serving trays. Welcome to the Weber family.
